 U Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for petitioner and S.S. Chauhan, Deputy Advocate General assisted by Mr. R.K. Joshi, Brief Holder for State of Uttarakhand.
2. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought following reliefs:-
"(a) Issue, Writ, Order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent no. 1 to 6 to provide adequate police protection to the petitioner and his employees and purchasers, from respondents no. 7, 8, 9, 10 and their followers and agents who are threatening the petitioner and his employees and purchasers by stopping them from entering or opening or buying the items from the shop. 
(b) issue, Writ, Order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing the respondent no. 1 to 6 to ensure that the respondent no. 7, 8, 9, 10 and their followers and agents shall not endanger the life and liberty of the petitioner and his employees and purchasers of his shop which is Your Daily Basket, Address of Authorised premises at A-3, Suddhowala, Vikas Nagar, Chakarata Road, PS Prem Nagar, Vikas Nagar, Dehradun. 
(c) Pass any other writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case. 
(d) Award the cost of the writ petition to the petitioner." 
3. According to petitioner, he was issued a license for running a grocery shop by Department of Food Safety, Government of Uttarakhand and he was also issued a license for retail sale of foreign liquor by Excise Department on 25.10.2024. It is further stated that a composite grocery and liquor shop has to be run from a rented accommodation, which he has taken on lease for a period of 5 years. 
WPCRL/1341/2024 on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161127491/
1 2024:UHC:9369-DB 4. The grievance raised by petitioner is that respondent Nos. 7, 8, 9 & 10 and some other persons residing in the locality are not permitting petitioner to run his business for which he has been issued license by competent authority. 
5. Learned State Counsel was asked to get instructions. Today, on instructions, he submits that police officials visited the place from where petitioner intends to run shop and during inspection, it was found that there are four rooms admeasuring 6 x 5 feet next to 2 feet wide gallery and it appears that petitioner intends to run a massage parlour and due to this residents of the locality are agitated and are opposing the petitioner. He however admits that petitioner possesses license for running grocery as well as liquor shop which was issued by the competent authority. 
6. Learned counsel for petitioner, on instructions, submitted that petitioner do not intend to run massage parlour and he gave an undertaking on behalf of his client that no massage parlour will ever be run from the premises in question. 
7. We, accordingly, dispose of this Writ Petition by directing Senior Superintendent of Police,
Dehradun (respondent No. 5), to ensure that no damage is caused to the shop of the petitioner and no demonstration, agitation, etc., is carried on within 100 meters of the premises from which petitioner proposes to run the shop.
